subject: Urgent: Request for vulnerability assessment and remediation detail
messages:
From: Nicole Torres <nicole@brightlinehealth.com>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com, sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 30 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Urgent: Request for vulnerability assessment and remediation detail

Olga / Sergio,

We flagged several anomalous API calls on our side last night tied to the integration between Brightline and Redwood (transaction IDs attached). Our security team is asking for the most recent penetration test report and a concise remediation/status summary for any findings that could relate to data-exposure or auth weaknesses.

Specifically we need: 1) the pen test report (even redacted) covering the last 12 months, 2) a short remediation matrix showing which findings are fixed vs in-progress and ETA, and 3) confirmation whether any of the recent findings overlap with items in your SOC 2 scope.

We appreciate urgency on this; our compliance lead is escalating this to procurement if we can’t validate controls quickly. If there’s someone else on your side we should talk to (infosec/legal), please loop them in.

Thanks,
Nicole Torres
Director of InfoSec Operations
Brightline Health
security@brightlinehealth.com

Attachments: Brightline-log-excerpt-0729.txt (text)
From: olga_petrov@redwood.com <olga_petrov@redwood.com>

Cc: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 30 Jul 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Urgent: Request for vulnerability assessment and remediation detail

Nicole — thanks for the heads up and the log excerpt. I’m sorry to hear you’re seeing anomalies. I’ve looped in Marissa from our security team to handle the pen test report and remediation summary.

Quick answers: we maintain SOC 2 and we have a penetration test from June 2026. We typically share a redacted version of the pen test for external customers; full reports are restricted. I’ll confirm what redaction level we can provide and expected turnaround.

Would you be available for a quick 30-min call today or tomorrow so Marissa can walk through the findings and remediation priorities? If you prefer, we can start by sharing a redacted PDF and a remediation checklist.

—Olga
Olga Petrov | Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Nicole — thanks for bringing this to our attention. I’m Sergio (Security Partner Liaison) — I’ll coordinate with our Infosec team and legal on sharing the pen test artifacts. A few points up front:

- Redwood performs an external penetration test annually; the latest was completed in June 2026.
- Our policy requires redaction of attack paths that would materially aid reproduction and removal of internal contact/credentials. We can provide a redacted report and a remediation matrix within 24–48 hours once we have a confirmed NDA/DPA amendment on file for sensitive attachments.
- If the request is strictly for high-level confidence (i.e., whether any findings map to SOC 2 in-scope systems), we can provide that mapping without the full redacted report immediately.

I’ve attached our redaction policy for transparency (redwood_pt_redaction_policy.pdf). If Brightline can sign the limited-sharing addendum (I’ll send a DocuSign link), we’ll push the redacted PDF and the remediation checklist to you. Otherwise, we can escalate to the compliance call.

Sergio Alvarez
Security Partner Liaison, Redwood Inference
sergio_alvarez@redwood.com

Available for a call today at 11:30 PT or 3:00 PT.

—Nicole

Nicole — thanks for the quick reply and offer to sign the addendum. Attached are: 1) Redwood-2026-06-PT-Report-redacted.pdf (we removed reproduction steps and internal hostnames), and 2) remediation-checklist-20260731.csv (finding id, severity, status, ETA). For transparency: none of the June 2026 findings indicate a token-exfiltration vector; the high/critical items were related to CSP misconfigurations and an outdated dependency in an internal telemetry worker (both fixed).

Summary of key remediation items we provided in the CSV:
- FIND-2026-014: CSP tightening — Completed (2026-07-15)
- FIND-2026-021: Telemetry worker dependency — Completed (2026-07-20)
- FIND-2026-030: Rate-limit edge case — In progress (ETA 2026-08-10) — mitigation: temporary throttling rule applied

We also mapped findings to SOC 2 in-scope services in the attached CSV (column: soc2_mapping). We’ve opened JIRA INC-4721 for the rate-limit work and included the ticket link in the CSV.

DocuSign: Sergio, I believe you sent the limited-sharing addendum earlier this morning; Brightline’s legal should receive it and sign electronically.

If you’d like a 20-minute walkthrough of the redacted report and checklist, I’m free today at 3:00 PT.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Head of Security Programs, Redwood Inference
